description: LASPATED fits nonhomogeneous Poisson models to events observed in space and time. Vincent Guigues and collaborators provide Python routines for discretizing observations and C++, MATLAB and Octave routines for estimating event intensities with regularisation or covariates. The own example combines Rio de Janeiro boundaries and medical emergency observations, while a New York example uses mock events. Geographic coverage, cell sizes and time intervals are user-defined. Estimated arrival rates can support ambulance-demand, fire-response or other service-capacity simulations. Public source code is free under BSD-3-Clause; the article archive has separate CC-BY-4.0 metadata. The model complements related dispatch or location optimisers by estimating their event-demand inputs. A limitation is the Poisson formulation and dependence on partition choices, observation completeness and calibration settings. The README distinguishes operating-system support for different languages. No emergency records, replication data or model estimates were downloaded or generated.
